options.text: A single element or component as it enters or leaves

questions.explanation: <Transition> animates one element/component on enter and leave (triggered by v-if, v-show, a dynamic component, or a key change). Lists use <TransitionGroup>.

questions.prompt: Which class should carry the CSS transition timing?
questions.explanation: The *-active classes are applied for the whole transition, so the transition/animation declaration goes there; *-from and *-to hold the start and end states.

questions.prompt: What does mode="out-in" achieve when swapping elements?

options.text: The leaving element finishes animating out before the entering one animates in

questions.explanation: out-in sequences the transition so the old content leaves completely before the new content enters, preventing an awkward overlap.

questions.prompt: To animate a list (adding, removing, reordering items), use <Transition______>. (complete the tag name)
questions.explanation: <TransitionGroup> animates lists; each child needs a stable key and reordering uses a *-move class.

questions.prompt: Why must <TransitionGroup> children have stable keys (not the index)?

options.text: Move/enter/leave animations rely on stable item identity; index keys change on reorder and break the animations

questions.explanation: Stable keys let Vue track which item moved where. Index keys shift on reorder, so Vue can't compute correct move transitions.

questions.prompt: Which can trigger a <Transition>? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: All four trigger enter/leave transitions: v-if, v-show, swapping a dynamic component, and a changing key.
